title: Development of an inventory for the early detection of depression in adulthood and youth – Depression Early Prediction Inventory
summary: It is crucial for those affected as well as for therapists and physicians to recognize depression at an early stage or to prevent its onset altogether. The aim of this study is therefore to develop an instrument to identify people at increased risk of developing depression. To this end, the so-called high-risk phase of depression—the period before the actual onset of the illness—is analyzed using interviews and questionnaires. Initial studies at the LVR Clinic in Düsseldorf have already shown that this high-risk phase is easy to detect. Therefore, the phase will now be examined more closely with a larger number of patients and comparison groups.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Patients with a previous or current diagnosis of a depressive disorder according to the ICD-10 /ICD-11/DSM-5 criteria:
a)	Depressive episode (ICD-10: F32.x / ICD-11: 6A70.x, 6A7Z / DSM-5: F32.x)
b)	Recurrent depressive disorder (ICD-10: F33.x / ICD-11: 6A71.x / DSM-5: F33.x)
c)	Bipolar affective disorder (ICD-10: F31.x / ICD-11: 6A6Z, 6A60.x / DSM-5: F31.x)
d)	Depressive conduct disorder (ICD-10: F92.0)
2.	Age between 13 and 65 years.
3.	The patient has sufficient verbal and cognitive abilities to understand and answer questions asked during the assessments.
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Insufficient knowledge of German that hinder the understanding of the questions and instructions 
2.	Acute suicidality 
3.	Comorbidities classified according to ICD-10 as:
a)	F0 Organic, including symptomatic, mental disorders
b)	F1 Mental and behavioural disorders due to psychoactive substance use (with the exception of the diagnosis F1x.1 "Harmful use" & diagnosis F17.2 "Mental and behavioral disorders due to use of tobacco: dependence syndrome")
c)	F2 Schizophrenia and delusional disorders (with the exception of the diagnosis F21: schizotypal disorder)
d)	F84 Pervasive developmental disorders
4.	History of severe somatic or neurological disease (e.g. tumor disease) with current influence on brain function 
5.	Learning disorder with effect on reading ability
6.	A medical history of somatic/neurological disease affecting the brain, which is the primary explanation for the psychological symptoms.
7.	Learning disability or intellectual disability (IQ < 70)
